M-G.text: A measurement may be relied upon only while the instrument's calibration is valid and its stated operating envelope is met, and the instrument must make both observable to the operator.
A reading within the declared uncertainty band of a decision threshold must trigger a defined repeat or confirmatory procedure before it is reported.
The admissible time window between disturbance and measurement must be stated for each analyte class and enforced by the procedure.
Sampling media and tooling must be qualified for the analyte class, and the qualification must be identifiable from the sample record.
A platform contamination limit must be defined beyond which further sampling is not valid.
An analytical result must be transmitted together with the criterion applied and the uncertainty of the measurement; a bare value is not a reportable result.
The provenance and validated scope of any advised criterion must accompany the advice.
The latency budget from measurement to result must be stated and must be shorter than the decision cycle it serves.
A determination that carries consequences for persons must rest on an instrument whose performance for that analyte and setting has been demonstrated against a stated standard.
A maximum time to determination must be defined, after which a default protective posture applies.
The determination must not precede completion of the confirmatory procedure that the reading triggered.
Defined changes of condition must re-open the determination.
Custody transfer must occur at recovery, before any decontamination, movement or re-tasking of the platform, and the interval must be recorded.
The period during which a machine holds a sample must itself be a recorded custody link, with the holder identified as the platform and its state logged.
Decontamination must not precede custody transfer.
A release criterion must be defined and met before the platform re-enters a clean area, and the release must be verifiable.
The sampling plan must map each ordered sample to a pre-established procedure and criterion; an unmapped sample must be flagged as such in the record.
Omission of an SOP-required sample must be recorded with its reason.
The conditions that trigger withdrawal must be defined in advance and must be observable from the feedback the operator actually receives.
A withdrawal order must carry a disposition for any sample and record already held.
Withdrawal thresholds must act on the projected time to reach a limit, not on the limit having been reached.
Entry may be commanded only with a platform established as decontaminable for the agent class in question, and the establishing evidence must be identifiable.
A dwell limit referenced to the platform's established tolerance must be defined and enforced.
The egress route and the decontamination point must be fixed before entry is commanded.
Stop authority must hold independently of the command link, and that independence must be demonstrated rather than asserted.
Stop behaviour must define the state of any sample held at the moment it executes.
Release from a stop must require an explicit human instruction.
A degraded-mode safe state must be defined so that recovery remains possible without exposing personnel.
Any sensor whose reading triggers a protective behaviour must be validated for the quantity and range in which that trigger sits.
The dropout duration that triggers the safe state must be stated and matched to the mission.

M-A.text: Flight over people may be conducted only with an aircraft demonstrated against a stated kinetic-energy limit and a stated rotor-exposure condition.
Sustained exposure of an assembly must be bounded by the condition that justified it.
The authorized purpose must be matched to a stated sensing capability; a purpose the payload cannot serve must not be authorized.
A change of purpose in flight must require re-authorization before the new sensing begins.
Any airspace condition imposed must be observable by the equipment carried, and the equipment's ability to meet it must be demonstrated before access is granted.
Withdrawal criteria for airspace access must be stated and monitored.
Imaging that can identify a person or the interior of a dwelling must be bound to a stated purpose, retention period and access rule at the moment it is commanded.
Recording must stop when the authorized subject is no longer the object of observation.
A recovery margin referenced to the population beneath must be defined and enforced.
Termination behaviour must account for the ground risk distribution, not only the aircraft.
Automatic behaviours must be constrained by the same spatial limits as commanded flight, and that constraint must be verifiable before flight.
Geofence data must be validated against the authorization before flight.
Custody of imagery must attach before any derived copy leaves the capture system.
Derived products must inherit the custody and retention rule of their source.

CC.text: Operator qualification must be demonstrated against the degraded conditions the mission actually presents, not only against nominal conditions.
Every control that must remain available in the contaminated zone must be actuatable in the protective equipment prescribed for that zone, and this must be verified with the equipment on.
What an instrument reports and what a decision needs must be distinguished on the display itself; where they differ the difference must be stated, not left to the reader's model.
Qualification to make the determination must include the instrument classes the criterion was validated on, and must be refreshed when the fielded instrument changes.
Calibration validity must be carried in the same feedback path as the reading it qualifies.
Any distinction the operator must make remotely has to be verifiable through the actual sensing and link path, not through direct inspection.
The custody entry required at recovery must be completable in the protective posture that recovery is conducted in.
Pilot qualification must include the distinction between airworthiness and operating-category eligibility, and must state which of the two the fielded route actually establishes.
Where an operator may self-certify, the content of that certification must be stated well enough that a refusal is possible.
The recorded field must not exceed the field the operator is shown.
Each stated withdrawal trigger must be bound to a feedback path that reaches the deciding authority within the mission.
A protective behaviour must be able to detect loss of trust in its own trigger input.
